claims.summary: 兒化音 is described for the Beijing sound system and some dialects; the attached 儿 is joined to the preceding syllable and makes its final retroflex.

sourceLinks.sourceTitle: 兒化音 — Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
sourceLinks.notes: Official definition: Beijing sound system and certain dialects; 儿 joins previous syllable and makes a retroflex final.

claims.summary: In erhua, the suffix 儿 does not form a separate syllable but merges with the preceding syllable; the transformation depends on the original final.

sourceLinks.sourceTitle: 兒化音 — Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
sourceLinks.notes: Official definition states the suffix does not form its own syllable and the preceding final becomes retroflex, with varying changes.

claims.summary: The official dictionary gives 花兒 as an example of the preceding 花 plus the suffix 兒 forming an erhua pronunciation.

sourceLinks.sourceTitle: 兒化音 — Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
sourceLinks.notes: The entry uses 花兒 to illustrate the merger of 花 and 兒.
Official dictionary confirms pronunciation and lexical identity of 花.

claims.summary: The source explicitly limits its description to Beijing phonology and certain dialects, so the entry avoids generalizing occurrence or frequency to all Mandarin or Taiwanese Mandarin; independent 儿 is distinct from an erhua suffix.

sourceLinks.sourceTitle: 兒化音 — Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
sourceLinks.notes: The source scope is Beijing phonology and some dialects, not all Mandarin varieties.
Official entry records 儿 as an independent lexical syllable as well as a suffix.

semanticReview.method: Manual review of each substantial statement against cited primary institutional source records

findings.supports: Manual comparison of each revised claim with the Ministry of Education dictionary entries for 兒化音, 兒, and 花; the article was narrowed to those documented definitions and example.

limitations: The dictionary is a reference entry and does not quantify erhua frequency across regions or document Taiwan usage; the article makes no such frequency claim.
